text:
Riley Chen: Morning team — quick onboarding Qs. 1) I added my domestic partner to benefits but Rippling requests "SSN for spouse". Partner is on an ITIN. Is that acceptable? 2) I enrolled in HSA but want to switch to HDHP + HSA from standard plan; can that be done mid-month? 3) I submitted a mileage reimbursement for moving help but haven't seen it processed.

Maya (People Ops): Welcome @Riley! Short answers: 1) An ITIN is acceptable for dependent verification — upload partner passport + ITIN documentation under Documents > Category: Benefits > Subtype: Dependent proof and tick "Share with Benefits Team". 2) Plan changes outside open enrollment typically require a qualifying life event. Adding a domestic partner counts as a QLE if you're adding them to coverage. We'll mark your case to allow changing to HDHP+HSA. 3) Mileage reimbursement should go to Finance; ensure you uploaded the expense form and mileage log under Documents > Category: Expenses > Subtype: Reimbursement.

Riley Chen: Thanks — I uploaded `riley_partner_itin.pdf` and a signed affidavit. Also, for HSA, if allowed midyear, what's the effective date and is the employer contribution pro-rated?

Tina (Benefits): If we process the QLE within 30 days of the qualifying event your HDHP+HSA can be effective as of your event date. Employer HSA contributions are prorated based on the remainder of the plan year. We'll update your ticket and follow up with exact pro-rate amount.

Jordan (Payroll): For mileage: reimbursements are taxable if not under accountable plan. If you filed the Accountable Expenses form and attached receipts, Finance posts it as "Mileage Reimbursement". Check ticket FIN-5597. If it's approved, it will be on the next payroll run. If you didn't use the mileage form, re-upload using the template here: https://intranet.redwood/expense-forms.

Benefits Bot: Ticket BZ-8822 created for dependent docs. Status: pending review.

Riley Chen: I used the mileage template and included Google's map screenshot. Uploaded under Expenses and attached FIN-5597 in the thread. One last nicety: I'm getting a "benefits overlap" msg since partner's employer also offers benefits. Any note on dual coverage coordination?

Maya (People Ops): Dual coverage is allowed but coordination of benefits is between carriers. If both plans are active, the carriers determine primary vs secondary. We can provide carrier ID cards and effective dates to your partner to give to their HR. Also, state-specific rules apply; if you want we can loop legal for guidance.

Riley Chen: Perfect — thanks everyone. I'll watch BZ-8822 and FIN-5597 and DM if they don't clear in 48h. :thumbsup:
